description: We are a team of high schoolers passionate about innovation, space travel, and the pursuit of knowledge.
summary:
We tackled this challenge by answering one question: how can landscapes on Earth help us interpret Martian surface processes, environmental conditions, and the future exploration of Mars? 

We built TerraLink, a 3D interactive platform aimed at advancing comparative planetary research. By connecting planetary datasets and terrestrial analog sites, our software accessibly compares temperature, glacial landscapes, evidence of past water structures, Aeolian process, potential habitability, mineralogy, and subsurface environments. Understanding their features are crucial to humanity’s future exploration of and presence on Mars. 

Users can explore planetary analog sites, find areas of interest, and learn about the similarities Mars and Earth share. TerraLink brings together NASA API, real, complex data, emerging places of interest on the Martian surface, and a love for planetary science that all users can share with ease.
details:
By innovatively integrating scientific datasets, NASA API, interactive geospatial tools, and our own original research, TerraLink enables users to investigate planetary environments through direct exploration and comparative analysis.

TerraLink combines several interconnected research capabilities within a unified platform:

Interactive 3D Planetary Visualization. Users can explore planetary landscapes through three-dimensional terrain visualization, examining surface morphology, elevation, and geological structures across Earth and Mars. This spatial perspective provides a more immersive way to investigate planetary features and their surrounding environments. Users can also view the 3D globes in a side-by-side view for easy comparison, as well as the “topology” mode and a 2D map view.

Comparative Weather and Environmental Analysis: TerraLink enables users to compare weather and environmental conditions across selected Earth and Mars locations. Examining variables such as temperature, weather, mineral composition, geological processes, and atmospheric conditions provides context for understanding the environmental similarities and differences between planetary analog sites that will greatly assist humanity for future Mars missions.

Custom Geographic Point Comparison: Rather than limiting users to predetermined comparisons, TerraLink incorporates custom point-based exploration, allowing users to select their own geographic locations and investigate their characteristics in relation to one another. This creates opportunities for identifying geological analogs beyond commonly studied or established locations.

Original Planetary Research Articles: TerraLink features in-depth, original research articles written by our team, investigating niche, emerging, and lesser-explored planetary analog sites. These articles connect scientific literature, geological observations, and environmental data to explain the significance of individual locations and their potential relevance to Martian research. By pairing original research with interactive visualization, users can move beyond identifying similarities to understanding the scientific processes and evidence behind them.

Intended Impact: Planetary research data is distributed across numerous scientific databases, mission archives, and specialized resources, often requiring technical expertise and multiple tools to interpret. TerraLink addresses this challenge by consolidating planetary exploration, comparative analysis, and scientific research within one accessible environment.

The intended impact of TerraLink extends far beyond conventional forms of education and visualization. TerraLink’s unique experience enables users to investigate unfamiliar or unknown locations, compare their environmental conditions, and explore the newly emerging terrestrial analogs. TerraLink encourages independent scientific inquiry, fosters curiosity and initiative, and offers plentiful opportunities for planetary discovery. Its research capabilities may also contribute to understanding geological processes on both worlds, evaluating potential environments for exploration and experimentation, and forming the enterprise of future human missions to Mars.

Creativity and Innovation: Our TerraLink sets itself apart through the complete integration of interactive 2D/3D exploration, customizable geographic comparisons, environmental and geological factor analysis, and the products of our original scientific research. Rather than presenting Earth–Mars analog relationships as fixed comparisons, the platform encourages users to investigate locations independently and explore geological connections that may not have been extensively studied.

The fusion of user-directed exploration and TerraLink’s custom-written research is particularly significant: users can discover and select a location, examine its environmental and geological characteristics, and continue on to access deeper scientific context about its relevance, similarities, and any divergent factors. This connects the probing of data with scientific inferences, elevating TerraLink from a conventional planetary visualization experience into an ascended platform for expansive research, thoughtful examinations, and nascent discoveries.

Development Considerations: Throughout the entire development process, our team carefully considered the scientific accuracy of our research, compatibility between our multiple datasets, as high of a degree of geographic position as possible, and the quality of our site’s visuals and total user experience. We prioritized chaining together information from different scientific sources while accounting for the fundamental difficulties inherent in comparing environments across planets. Differences in gravity, atmospheric pressure and composition, radiation levels, and other features distinct to the planet itself must be accounted for when evaluating terrestrial analogs. As for the features common between analogs, such as geographic location, elevation, wind levels, temperature, and mineral chemical composition, these were carefully analyzed in our selection of analogous locations. 

Ultimately, our team and TerraLink possess a deep-seated aspiration to make planetary research more interwoven, accessible, and investigative. By assimilating scientific data, interactive tools, cutting-edge technologies, and original research, we hope to encourage users of TerraLink to discover and ruminate upon geological relationships between Earth and Mars and contribute to a broader understanding of our planetary environments!

-- The Project Minerva Team
